Subject: New vendor onboarding — PO tags and spend cap question

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're excited to get Dockable onto Redwood. I started filling the onboarding packet but ran into a couple of things that may block our procurement team:

- The onboarding form asks for a single PO number, but our AP needs line-level PO mapping (we have three product SKUs on our first invoice).
- The spend cap in the portal defaulted to $25k for the account — that is below the committed onboarding budget.

I attached the onboarding form and a quick CSV with the planned invoice lines. Could we get guidance on how Redwood issues PO numbers for multi-SKU onboarding and whether we can bump the spend cap to $75k for the initial quarter?

Appreciate any help — looping in Carlos from our procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Head of Finance Operations
Dockable Inc.

Attachments: dockable_onboarding_form_v3.pdf (application/pdf), ponum_lineitems_v1.csv (text/csv)

Thanks Lina — good details.

Quick summary of what we need to resolve internally:
1) PO issuance model for multi-line invoices (do we provide a single PO with line tags, or serialized sub-POs?)
2) Temporary spend cap increase for onboarding (Lina requests $75k for Q4 onboarding)
3) Ensure vendor form maps SKUs to our ledger codes so invoices reconcile.

Monica: can you confirm the current policy for PO serials on vendor onboarding and whether we can provision a provisional pooled PO that supports line tagging?
Markus: if we can do the provisional cap increase, what approval path/timeframe do we need?
Priyom: if we end up issuing sub-POs, can the provisioning workflow set them as children of the main onboarding PO so finance sees the rollup?

I'll hold on replying to Dockable until we have the plan.

- Tessa
Director, Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for pulling this together. Quick answers from procurement side:

- Current default is a single PO number per onboarding, with free-text line descriptions. We introduced a "PO tag" convention earlier this year so AP can map multiple invoice lines to sub-ledger codes, but the portal currently doesn't auto-serialize PO children.
- We can create a provisional grouped PO that includes a PO-level tag header and explicit per-line reference codes. That will require a manual entry in the procure system (about 24 hours) and a brief note to AP so they route invoices correctly.

Two asks from me before I create the provisional grouped PO:
- Confirm the exact ledger codes for the three SKUs (Lina's CSV lists them as SKUs A/B/C but no ledger codes).
- We need procurement approval to raise the temporary spend cap to $75k; would prefer a written request from Finance for audit trail.

If Finance sends the approval email, I can create the grouped PO and add per-line reference strings that match AP's import.

Monica
Senior Procurement Analyst
Redwood Inference

- SKU C -> LEDGER-4014

Carlos will send a brief email confirming the $75k temporary increase. I'm happy to get on a 15-min call if that's easier.

Lina

Following up with a proposed operational approach that minimizes manual reconciliation: 

1) Issue a master onboarding PO: PO-ONB-20250917-DOCK (single visible PO number).
2) Create three sub-PO reference strings for AP import: PO-ONB-20250917-DOCK-A, -B, -C. These are not separate payable POs but are tagged child references that AP can map to lines.
3) Add a PO-level memo with the ledger mapping (LEDGER-4012/4013/4014) and include the CSV as the canonical line mapping.
4) Provisionally raise the spend cap to $75,000 for 90 days; track on PROC-314 and auto-revert unless extended with written approval.

If procurement & finance approve, I can run the provisioning and add the child tags to the PO. Once done I'll reply with the issued PO number and the three child reference strings.

Priyom
